scenes.headline: How a model learns to say how sure it is
scenes.sub: RLCD: Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions, the method behind TypeSafe's Jev.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Noodle! RLCD means reinforcement learning for calibrated decisions, not constrained decoding. It's how TypeSafe says it trains Jev, a model that never writes text.

scenes.label: The contract
scenes.text: The model returns a decision and a probability, never text. Answers given 0.8 should turn out right about 80% of the time.
scenes.say: The contract: the model returns a decision and a probability, never text. Answers given point eight should be right about eighty percent of the time.

steps.note: a Choice, a Score, or a single probability
steps.say: The caller supplies the options at request time, up to two hundred and fifty-five, and the model has never seen them before.

steps.note: an open reproduction's head; Jev's is undisclosed
steps.say: In an open reproduction, a small head reads the question and one option together, and outputs a single number. Once per option.
A softmax across that question's options turns those numbers into probabilities. Jev probably works this way too, though its head is undisclosed.

left.title: A linear penalty
left.say: Score a report by its plain distance from the outcome, and a model that believes seventy percent does best by claiming certainty.

right.title: A proper scoring rule
right.say: A proper scoring rule, like cross-entropy or Brier, is minimised by reporting your true belief. The open reproductions train on both, added together.

scenes.label: calibration error of GPT-4, before and after preference optimization
scenes.note: TypeSafe publishes no loss, reward, data or calibration number
scenes.say: Pretrained models are already well calibrated when choosing among options. Preference tuning made GPT-4's calibration error ten times worse. TypeSafe publishes no method or calibration number at all.

scenes.text: Calibration probably comes less from a new algorithm than from a proper scoring rule, and from not doing what breaks it.

recap: A decision and a probability, never text
One scalar per option, then a softmax
Proper scoring rules make honesty cheapest
scenes.say: To recap: decisions, not text; one score per option; and a loss that makes the honest probability the cheapest one.
